cooler than the bedroom) satisfied crossvent <= 1 and was labelled STALLED /

commits.headline: fix(d1-sync): dead-letter FK orphans, bisect failed batches, alarm on queue depth (#831)
commits.body:
## Why
The D1 outbox push path is FK-fragile. Local `hub-unified.db` runs
`foreign_keys=OFF` and accumulates orphaned/out-of-order rows, while
`workers/d1-sync-proxy` applies each batch atomically with FKs
**enforced** on D1. One orphan child row (parent never synced) FK-failed
the whole batch — and because FK errors never burned an attempt, the row
cycled forever (`dead=0`). `sync_queue` never drained, bloating the DB
to 2.49GB over ~7 weeks (incident a984cd2f).

commits.body:
## Why
The worker returns null sub-cursors for any table with no new rows in a
tick. The reconciler wrote those verbatim, clobbering a
previously-advanced cursor back to null and resetting reconciliation to
the beginning — leaving `d1_reconcile_last_cursor` effectively null, so
the parity backstop never made progress (incident a984cd2f).

commits.headline: fix(d1-sync): defer foreign-key enforcement in the sync worker batch (#832)
commits.body:
## Why
D1 runs each `batch()` in an implicit transaction with foreign keys
enforced per-statement, so a child row that precedes its parent **inside
the same batch** fails with `FOREIGN KEY` and rolls the whole batch back
— the intra-batch ordering fragility behind incident a984cd2f.

commits.headline: fix: self-terminate orphaned stdio MCP servers to stop a memory leak (#137)
commits.body:
The stdio MCP server had no path to exit when its client disconnected
while idle. When an intermediate wrapper (npx -> npm exec -> node bin ->
server) held the server's stdin write-end open, a dead client never
delivered EOF and the leaf lingered in the event loop forever — ~108 MB
each. On this machine 155 had accumulated, reparented to PID 1, for
~18 GB of leaked RSS.
